Docs/Training & baselines

Training & baselines

Choose a baseline, preserve the data and control contract, and distinguish paper results from research entry points.

Choose the learning setting

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

The manuscript evaluates six baselines: PPO, RLPD, ACT, Diffusion Policy, GR00T N1.7 and π0.5. They cover demonstration-guided reinforcement learning, imitation learning and vision-language-action adaptation. More algorithms exist in the research tree, but those entry points are not additional scored manuscript baselines.

Before training, fix the canonical task, source revision, episode split, observation schema, cameras, instruction rule and absolute joint-target contract. Preserve the resolved trainer configuration and dataset identity with each checkpoint.

Prepare data and configuration together

Use utils/dex_tasks.py and task/config/collection_targets.py to resolve the task rather than inheriting a trainer's generic default environment. Match --env-id, --control-mode and the dataset/task configuration together. Some research defaults target unrelated ManiSkill tasks and are not DexArena presets.

ACT and Diffusion Policy use preprocessed image datasets and camera/state mappings. GR00T needs its VLA dataset conversion, modality configuration and compatible base weights. Reinforcement-learning runs need the demonstration loader and reset-state assumptions to match the task. Check train/TRAIN_EVAL.md and the corresponding train/train_configs/ file before starting a run.

python -m train.train_ACT --help
python -m train.train_DP --help
python -m train.train_ppo --help
python -m train.train_rlpd --help
python -m train.train_groot --help

These help commands inspect the research entry points; they are not a complete installation or reproduction recipe. Model packages, datasets and assets must already be present.

The six evaluated methods

PPO

The DexArena baseline augments PPO with behavior-cloning warm-up, behavior-cloning regularization, demonstration-state resets and demonstration-informed action statistics. Rewards are sparse task-success rewards. The reported PPO budget is one million environment steps per stage; the step-zero point of its training curves follows the cloning warm-up.

Inspect train/train_ppo.py, train/train_configs/ppo_config.py and algo/ppo.py. Record the warm-up, reset distribution and training budget alongside the final checkpoint. Original paper ↗

RLPD

The paper's offline-to-online baseline mixes equal portions of demonstration samples and online replay samples. Keep the demonstration dataset fixed while collecting online transitions, and record both sample sources and the update budget.

Inspect train/train_rlpd.py, train/train_configs/rlpd_config.py and algo/offline_to_online_rl/rlpd.py. Other SAC/OPT entry points in the tree do not automatically reproduce the manuscript's RLPD configuration. ICML 2023 paper ↗

ACT

Action Chunking with Transformers predicts sequences of arm and hand targets from visual and state observations. The DexArena baseline balances reconstruction losses for the arm and hand. Match the dataset's cameras, policy-state selection, action normalization and chunk execution rule during evaluation.

Inspect train/train_ACT.py and train/train_configs/ACT_config.py. This trainer exposes explicit camera mappings, state adapters and inference modes; save the selected values instead of relying on automatic matching across a changed dataset. Original ALOHA / ACT project ↗

Diffusion Policy

The image-based diffusion baseline predicts arm and hand joint-action chunks from temporal multi-view observations. The implemented image path uses absolute actions. Keep the observation history, predicted chunk size, executed action count and diffusion configuration in the checkpoint manifest.

Inspect train/train_DP.py, train/train_configs/DP_config.py and algo/diffusion.py. The current DP configuration supports chunk inference and validates its architecture/action settings. Original project & paper ↗

GR00T N1.7

DexArena adapts GR00T with embodiment-specific state/action encoding and task language. Its adapter converts relative arm offsets into absolute controller targets while keeping finger targets absolute. The paper uses full-model fine-tuning on task demonstrations.

Inspect train/train_groot.py, train/train_configs/groot_config.py and algo/groot.py. Set explicit local paths for the compatible base model, converted VLA dataset and modality configuration; research-machine default paths are not public downloads. Use Quick evaluation to check a compatible checkpoint. Official NVIDIA repository ↗

π0.5

The manuscript evaluates stage-specific policies and composes them by switching on stage success without a simulator reset. Report the policy selected for each stage and the switching rule so complete-sequence results can be interpreted.

Research entry points include train/train_pi05_sft.py, train/train_pi05_grpo.py and train/eval_pi05.py. Their current configurations include task-specific experimental contracts: the inspected SFT default is a Franka peg-insertion setup with end-effector actions, not a generic Sharpa joint-space recipe. Do not run those defaults as a reproduction of the DexArena π0.5 table. A matching stage-specific model/data configuration is required. Official Physical Intelligence report ↗

Turn a training run into a comparable result

  1. Save the source, dataset and preprocessing revisions, episode splits, random seeds and full resolved configuration.
  2. Select a checkpoint using the declared validation rule; keep held-out native scenes separate from checkpoint selection.
  3. Freeze the selected checkpoint and adapter before evaluating all task/scene/seed combinations.
  4. Evaluate complete sequences with one initial reset and the declared stage-composition rule.
  5. Export per-episode results and compute the task-weighted aggregates from those records.

Training curves describe learning progress; they do not replace the frozen-checkpoint evaluation. The primary method links above describe the original algorithms. DexArena-specific adaptations are described in the manuscript and these research interfaces.

Evaluate the frozen checkpoint

Continue with Policy integration, Scene evaluation and the score protocol. Cite DexArena and the original methods you use; the citation guide provides the benchmark reference.
